name: Interlock
description: Interlock (EEA Tokenization Starter Kit): regulated tokens from different institutions working together on Ethereum, with FINOS CDM for settlement instructions and results.

nodes.name: Interlock toolkit
nodes.description: The off-chain part of Interlock: the core library, product templates, example console and CLI, recorder and demo site.

nodes.name: Interlock contracts
nodes.description: The on-chain part of Interlock: RegulatedToken (one per product), the default ShibuiEligibility slot and DvPSettlement.

nodes.name: Ethereum network
nodes.description: A local Ethereum node (anvil) by default, or the Sepolia testnet with one setting. Ethereum mainnet is refused.

mainnet-refused.description: The chain id is checked on connect, in deploy and before every signature; chain id 1 is refused before any transaction.

config.name: Mainnet refused
config.description: The chain id is checked on connect, in deploy and before every signature; chain id 1 is refused before any transaction.

nodes.name: RegulatedToken
nodes.description: One ERC-20 contract for every product, with issue, redeem, freeze, forced transfer and pause. Asks its eligibility slot before every balance change. Deployed once per product template.

fail-closed.description: A reverting, missing or malformed eligibility answer means not eligible; the ERC-7943 views never revert.

config.name: Fail closed
config.description: A reverting, missing or malformed eligibility answer means not eligible; the ERC-7943 views never revert.

no-product-specific-code.description: Products differ only in their template file; the token has no product logic.

config.name: No product-specific code
config.description: Products differ only in their template file; the token has no product logic.

nodes.name: ShibuiEligibility
nodes.description: Default eligibility slot. Enforcement is Shibui isVerified, unchanged; explain replays the per-topic check to give a reason such as "accreditation: policy rejected".

enforcement-separate-from-explanation.description: The explanation is a read-only view and can never weaken enforcement.

config.name: Enforcement separate from explanation
tests: test/integration (I9: explain agrees with isVerified after every state change)
config.description: The explanation is a read-only view and can never weaken enforcement.

nodes.name: OnChainTrust VleiEligibility
nodes.description: Second eligibility slot, pinned and unmodified: a wallet is eligible when it holds a live vLEI attestation from the OnChainTrust bridge.

nodes.name: EEA Shibui
nodes.description: Eligibility layer of the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance, pinned at commit 4414538 and unmodified: per-token verifier, topics registry, trusted attesters and topic policies (KYC, AML, sanctions, country, accreditation).

nodes.name: Ethereum Attestation Service
nodes.description: Where KYC providers and the vLEI bridge issue and revoke credentials. The real EAS contracts run locally; the public EAS is reused on Sepolia.

nodes.name: DvPSettlement
nodes.description: Generic delivery-versus-payment contract: both legs move in one transaction or neither does. Never holds tokens, so each token checks the real sender and recipient.

atomic-settlement.description: Both legs or neither; balances conserved; the contract never holds a balance.

config.name: Atomic settlement
config.description: Both legs or neither; balances conserved; the contract never holds a balance.

nodes.name: OnChainTrust vLEI-to-EAS bridge
nodes.description: External bridge that turns GLEIF vLEI credentials into EAS attestations and revokes them when the credential or LEI stops being valid. A local test bridge with fictional banks is used for the recording.

nodes.name: Interlock core
nodes.description: Node library: deployer, action library and conformance suites. Bring your own signer, or prepare unsigned transactions. No demo cast and no keys.

bring-your-own-signer.description: Institutions sign with their own custody (HSM, MPC, custodian); the core holds no keys.

config.name: Bring your own signer
config.description: Institutions sign with their own custody (HSM, MPC, custodian); the core holds no keys.

nodes.name: Product templates
nodes.description: One JSON file per product (name, symbol, required topics, trusted attesters, country and accreditation rules, eligibility source), validated against schemas/ before any transaction.

nodes.name: FINOS CDM TransferInstruction
nodes.description: FINOS Common Domain Model 7.10.0 cdm.event.common.TransferInstruction: an Instructed two-leg instruction drives settlement, and comes back Settled with the transaction hash. Every token movement is exported the same way. Validated with the finos-cdm package.

cdm-drives-settlement.description: Settlement is driven by a CDM instruction and answered in CDM; CDM does not drive issuance in this round.

config.name: CDM drives settlement and receives the answer
config.description: Settlement is driven by a CDM instruction and answered in CDM; CDM does not drive issuance in this round.

nodes.name: Example console and CLI
nodes.description: Quickstart server, web console and command-line tool built on the core. Holds the public test keys of the local chain on the server; no key reaches the browser.

keys-server-side.description: Keys stay on the server side in the examples; responses never contain a key.

config.name: Keys stay on the server side
config.description: Keys stay on the server side in the examples; responses never contain a key.

nodes.name: Recorder
nodes.description: examples/record.mjs runs the demo stories through the core against the real contracts and writes the recording; every expected outcome is asserted.

nodes.name: Demo recording
nodes.description: web/data: every step, result, refusal reason, transaction hash and state, plus the CDM objects. Nothing in it is hand-written.

nodes.name: Demo site
nodes.description: Static page on GitHub Pages that plays the recording back: three products, settlement between instruments, vLEI, and the CDM view.

nodes.name: Issuer
nodes.description: A bank, fund manager or private credit firm that issues and redeems its product (fictional in the demo).

nodes.name: Compliance officer
nodes.description: Freezes, forces transfers and pauses a product.

nodes.name: Investor
nodes.description: Holds and transfers tokens when every product rule is met.

nodes.name: KYC provider
nodes.description: Issues one credential per investor, registers it with each product, and revokes it.

nodes.name: Operator
nodes.description: Deploys products from templates and authorizes KYC providers, leaving an on-chain audit trail.

nodes.name: Back office
nodes.description: Post-trade and operations team that instructs settlement and reads results in FINOS CDM.

flows.name: Transfer checked by eligibility
flows.description: An investor transfers a token; the token asks its slot about sender and recipient, and the transfer is refused with a reason by topic when a rule fails.

transitions.description: The investor asks to transfer
The core simulates, then sends the transfer
The token asks: may sender and recipient hold this?
Shibui checks every required topic
Each credential is read from EAS
Yes moves the balance; no reverts with an ERC-7943 error, and explain gives the topic

flows.name: Revoke once, blocked everywhere
flows.description: A KYC provider revokes a credential on EAS, and the next transfer on every product is refused.

transitions.description: The KYC provider revokes the credential on EAS
The investor tries the next transfer
The token asks its slot
Shibui finds the credential revoked
EAS reports the revocation time

flows.name: Delivery versus payment from a CDM instruction
flows.description: The back office sends a CDM TransferInstruction; both legs settle in one transaction under each token's own rules, and the instruction comes back Settled.

transitions.description: An Instructed CDM TransferInstruction with two legs
The core parses and checks the instruction
One settle call
transferFrom on the delivery and the payment token
Each token checks its own rules; a refusal reverts both legs
The instruction returns Settled with the transaction hash

flows.name: An institution recognised by its vLEI
flows.description: A bank wallet holding a live vLEI attestation becomes eligible for an institutional product through the OnChainTrust slot.

transitions.description: The bridge attests the bank's vLEI credential on EAS
A payment to the bank
The token asks the vLEI slot
Live, unexpired, right schema, attester and credential type
